Steps to Reproduce: 1. Launch Postman.`n2. Create a POST request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users.`n3. Under Body select raw -> JSON and input an empty JSON object: {}.`n4. Click Send.
Expected Result: The API should return HTTP 400 Bad Request with a message indicating mandatory fields ('name', 'email') are missing.
Actual Result: The API returns HTTP 201 Created with body: { "id": 11 }, accepting an empty record without any validation.

Steps to Reproduce: 1. Launch Postman.`n2. Create a POST request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users.`n3. Under Body select raw -> JSON and input an invalid email string.`n4. Click Send.
Expected Result: The API should validate the email format and return HTTP 400 Bad Request with an error description (e.g. 'Invalid email address format').
Actual Result: The API returns HTTP 201 Created with body: { "name": "Test User", "email": "not-an-email-address", "id": 11 }, accepting corrupted data formats.
Evidence: Response Status: 201 Created with invalid email preserved

Steps to Reproduce: 1. Launch Postman.`n2. Create a POST request to https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users.`n3. Under Body select raw -> JSON and input malformed JSON without closing bracket or quotes.`n4. Click Send.
Expected Result: The server should gracefully catch client request parsing failures and return HTTP 400 Bad Request (Client Error).
Actual Result: The server throws an unhandled SyntaxError resulting in HTTP 500 Internal Server Error.
Evidence: Response Status: 500 Internal Server Error (SyntaxError: Unexpected token n in JSON at position 1)
